loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

2872:model ReferralPartner {
2873-  id                String              @id @default(cuid())
2874-  // Optional login account the partner uses to view their portal at
2875-  // /dashboard/partner. A partner may exist purely as an admin-managed record
2876-  // (no login) until they self-serve. SetNull so deleting the user keeps history.
2877-  userId            String?             @unique
2878-  user              User?               @relation("PartnerAccount", fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
2879-  name              String
2880-  contactEmail      String?
2881-  code              String              @unique
2882-  // Lifetime commission rate (percent of the NET, pre-tax charge) earned on every
2883-  // qualifying charge by every attached customer.
2884-  commissionRatePct Float               @default(20)
2885-  status            String              @default("ACTIVE") // ACTIVE | PAUSED
2886-  notes             String?
2887-  createdAt         DateTime            @default(now())
2888-  customers         PartnerCustomer[]
2889-  commissions       PartnerCommission[]
2890-  /// What KIND of partner this is: agency | kol | community | developer |
2891-  /// reseller. Display only — the commission rate is `commissionRatePct` and
2892-  /// is not derived from this. Null on partners linked before the field existed.
2893-  type              String?
2894-}
2895-
2896-/// The durable link binding a referred customer to their referring partner for the
2897-/// life of the account. `customerId` is UNIQUE: a customer is attached to exactly
2898-/// ONE partner, permanently — the "lifetime attribution" guarantee.
2899:model PartnerCustomer {
2900-  id         String          @id @default(cuid())
2901-  partnerId  String
2902-  partner    ReferralPartner @relation(fields: [partnerId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
2903-  customerId String          @unique
2904-  customer   User            @relation("PartnerAttachment", fields: [customerId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
2905-  attachedAt DateTime        @default(now())
2906-  createdAt  DateTime        @default(now())
2907-
2908-  @@index([partnerId])
2909-}
2910-
2911-/// One commission entry per qualifying charge. `invoiceId` is UNIQUE — this is the
2912-/// idempotency guard: at most one commission row can ever exist per invoice, so a
2913-/// retried/duplicated accrual (inline hook + background sweep) can never double-pay
2914-/// a partner. `baseCents` and `ratePct` are snapshotted at accrual so the ledger is
2915-/// a durable record independent of later rate changes.
2916:model PartnerCommission {
2917-  id          String          @id @default(cuid())
2918-  partnerId   String
2919-  partner     ReferralPartner @relation(fields: [partnerId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
2920-  customerId  String
2921-  customer    User            @relation("PartnerCommissions", fields: [customerId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
2922-  invoiceId   String          @unique
2923-  invoice     Invoice         @relation(fields: [invoiceId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
2924-  // Net (pre-tax) charge the commission was computed on, the frozen rate, and the
2925-  // resulting commission — all snapshotted at accrual.
2926-  baseCents   Int
2927-  ratePct     Float
2928-  amountCents Int
2929-  kind        String          @default("CHARGE") // ORDER | RENEWAL | CHARGE
2930-  status      String          @default("ACCRUED") // ACCRUED | PAID | VOID
2931-  createdAt   DateTime        @default(now())
2932-  paidAt      DateTime?
2933-
2934-  @@index([partnerId, status])
2935-  @@index([customerId])
2936-}
2937-

2939-model Testimonial {
2940-  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
2941-  author      String
2942-  role        String?
2943-  quote       String
2944-  avatarEmoji String?
2945-  rating      Int      @default(5)
2946-  published   Boolean  @default(false)
2947-  sortOrder   Int      @default(0)
2948-  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
2949-}
2950-

1	import { vpsTerm, vpsTermPriceCents, termPriceCents } from "./billing-terms";
2	import { extraDiskCentsAt } from "./extra-disk";
3	import { type BackupTier, backupTierMonthlyCents } from "./backup-tiers";
4	
5	/**
6	 * What one renewal costs — the SINGLE definition, used by every path that quotes
7	 * or charges one: the automatic sweep in worker/billing.ts, the saved-card path,
8	 * the "Renew now" button, the server page and the deploy wizard's term cards.
9	 *
10	 * WHY IT LIVES IN ITS OWN FILE. It used to sit in lib/stripe-cards.ts, which
11	 * imports the Stripe SDK and (transitively) nodemailer. The moment a CLIENT
12	 * component — the deploy wizard — needed the renewal price, that import chain
13	 * dragged `nodemailer/lib/dkim` into the browser bundle and the build failed with
14	 * "Can't resolve 'fs'". The pricing rule is pure arithmetic and has no business
15	 * carrying a mail transport with it, so it lives here with only the two tiny
16	 * modules it genuinely needs. lib/stripe-cards.ts re-exports it, so no server-side
17	 * caller had to change.
18	 *
19	 * The rule this file exists to enforce: there is ONE renewal formula. Two
20	 * incidents in one day came from a second copy — first a button that hardcoded
21	 * "+30 days" and the monthly price while the action charged a full term ($8.99
22	 * shown, $97.09 taken), then the shared quote written to fix it, which computed
23	 * from `plan.priceCents` and so ignored `gamePlan` and would have billed a $4.99
24	 * game server at its $8.99 base plan. Do not add a second formula.
25	 */
26	export type RenewalCharge = {
27	  months: number;
28	  /**
29	   * The amount to CHARGE / display — tax-INCLUSIVE (net + tax). When no
30	   * `taxRatePercent` is supplied (the default), tax is 0 and this equals `netCents`,
31	   * so every existing caller is unchanged. Because display and charge both read this
32	   * one field, `displayed === charged === renewed` holds by construction.
33	   */
34	  totalCents: number;
35	  /** The pre-tax subtotal (plan + IP + disk + backup). Invoice line items sum to this. */
36	  netCents: number;
37	  /** The VAT/GST added on top of `netCents` (Finding 1); 0 when no rate was passed. */
38	  taxCents: number;
39	  /** The rate (%) `taxCents` was computed at, recorded on the invoice. */
40	  taxRatePercent: number;
41	  /** The extra-root-disk portion, which gets its own invoice line. */
42	  extraDiskCents: number;
43	  extraDiskMonthlyCents: number;
44	  /** The paid backup-tier portion (Plus retention), which gets its own invoice line. */
45	  backupCents: number;
46	  backupMonthlyCents: number;
47	  /**
48	   * How much of `netCents` was shaved off by a one-time RETENTION OFFER
49	   * (`PricedServer.pendingRenewalDiscountPercent`) on THIS renewal. 0 for every
50	   * server that never went through the cancel-flow retention offer (the
51	   * overwhelming majority) — existing callers that never read this field see no
52	   * behavior change. Exists so the invoice can show the discount as its own
53	   * line, the same way `extraDiskCents`/`backupCents` get their own lines,
54	   * instead of silently folding it into a smaller plan line.
55	   */
56	  retentionDiscountCents: number;
57	  /** Human label for the invoice / receipt ("Nebula VPS" or the game plan name). */
58	  label: string;
59	};
60	
61	export type PricedServer = {
62	  termMonths: number;
63	  extraDiskGB: number;
64	  plan: { name: string; priceCents: number };
65	  gamePlan: { name: string; priceCents: number; termMonths: number } | null;
66	  dedicatedIp: unknown | null;
67	  /**
68	   * Did the customer actually choose/pay for this IP, vs. a VPS just being
69	   * handed one for free by the `dedicated_ip_default` platform setting? See the
70	   * IP surcharge lines below for why this has to gate the charge alongside
71	   * `dedicatedIp` itself.
72	   */
73	  wantsDedicatedIp: boolean;
74	  /** Paid backup retention tier. A full Server row supplies it; synthetic callers must pass it. */
75	  backupTier: BackupTier;
76	  /**
77	   * The ANNUAL discount FROZEN on this server at sale (`Server.annualDiscountPct`),
78	   * or null on a legacy/monthly/flat row. OPTIONAL so the many synthetic
79	   * `PricedServer` display/quote objects keep compiling; a full Server row supplies
80	   * it automatically. When present it WINS over the live `prices.annualDiscountPct`,
81	   * so an annual VPS / NxCloud / game server renews at exactly the rate it was
82	   * SOLD at even if the admin retunes the setting afterwards; null falls back to
83	   * the live rate, which for every non-annual term is identical maths.
84	   */
85	  annualDiscountPct?: number | null;
86	  /**
87	   * GRANDFATHER PROGRAM (2026-09-17): the plan/game-plan monthly rate FROZEN
88	   * on this server at sale (`Server.grandfatheredRenewalCents`), read here
89	   * INSTEAD OF the live `plan.priceCents` / `gamePlan.priceCents` when
90	   * present. OPTIONAL, same shape as `annualDiscountPct` above — every
91	   * existing synthetic `PricedServer` (wizard previews, tests) keeps
92	   * compiling and keeps pricing off the live catalog rate exactly as
93	   * before; only a real Server row (which supplies it automatically)
94	   * actually grandfathers anything. Null/undefined = price off the live
95	   * plan, which is correct for a legacy pre-program row that was never
96	   * backfilled AND for a free/admin server with no real price to freeze.
97	   */
98	  grandfatheredRenewalCents?: number | null;
99	  /**
100	   * RETENTION OFFER (2026-09-17 field, wired 2026-09-19): the one-time percent
101	   * FROZEN on this server's `pendingRenewalDiscountPercent` when a customer
102	   * accepted the "stay and save" cancel-flow offer (lib/actions-server-lifecycle.ts
103	   * claimRetentionOffer). Unlike `grandfatheredRenewalCents` (a permanent
104	   * per-month price override), this discounts exactly ONE upcoming renewal
105	   * charge and the caller is responsible for clearing it back to null once that
106	   * renewal actually commits (see worker/billing.ts commitRenewal and
107	   * lib/actions.ts renewNow) — `renewalCharge` itself only reads it, it never
108	   * decides when the discount has been "used up". OPTIONAL / null = no pending
109	   * discount, which is every server that has never gone through the retention
110	   * flow (and is therefore identical to today's behavior).
111	   */
112	  pendingRenewalDiscountPercent?: number | null;
113	};
114	
115	/**
116	 * The admin-priced inputs a renewal is charged against. Every field is REQUIRED
117	 * deliberately, mirroring how the codebase guards renewal pricing everywhere else
118	 * (`termPromoPercent` is likewise required in lib/proration.ts): a call site that
119	 * builds this object cannot silently forget one and fall back to a stale default.
120	 */
121	export type RenewalPrices = {
122	  ipMonthlyCents: number;
123	  extraDiskPerGbCents: number;
124	  backupPlusCents: number;
125	  /**
126	   * The admin-configured ANNUAL discount (percent), resolved from the
127	   * `annual_discount_percent` setting via `annualDiscountPct()`.
128	   *
129	   * REQUIRED — not optional. A 12-month server renews at
130	   * `vpsTermPriceCents(price, 12, annualDiscountPct)`; if a call site could OMIT
131	   * this it would silently price annual at the shipped default (10%) while the
132	   * owner had set, say, 20% — the rate the customer was shown and charged at order.
133	   * Required turns that into a compile error at every one of the ~8 places that
134	   * build this object, so the annual setting cannot be forgotten on any renewal
135	   * path and `displayed === charged === renewed` holds.
136	   */
137	  annualDiscountPct: number;
138	  /**
139	   * OPTIONAL destination VAT/GST rate (percent) for the customer who owns this
140	   * server, resolved from their billing country (lib/tax.ts taxContextForUser).
141	   * Omitted / 0 => no tax added and `totalCents === netCents`, so every call site
142	   * that does not opt in is byte-for-byte unchanged. A charge site passes the
143	   * OWNER's rate so the wallet debit, the card leg and the invoice all agree; a
144	   * display of the owner's own renewal passes the SAME rate so the figure shown
145	   * equals the figure taken.
146	   */
147	  taxRatePercent?: number;
148	};
149	
150	export function renewalCharge(
151	  server: PricedServer,
152	  prices: RenewalPrices,
153	): RenewalCharge {
154	  const isGame = !!server.gamePlan;
155	  // The term to renew — the customer's chosen `Server.termMonths` (1 = monthly,
156	  // 12 = annual). A game term is now a per-order choice (Monthly / Annual) just like
157	  // a VPS, so it rides the Server row, not the plan.
158	  //
159	  // VPS/NxCloud terms are always one of the 4 standard `VPS_TERMS`, so we normalise
160	  // through `vpsTerm`. A GAME server, however, may historically carry ANY term the
161	  // plan was configured with (a pre-existing game server was created with
162	  // `termMonths = gamePlan.termMonths`, which the admin can set 1..36). We therefore
163	  // read the game term back RAW (clamped >= 1) rather than through `vpsTerm`, whose
164	  // fallback would collapse a non-standard legacy value (say 3) to monthly and
165	  // change that server's renewal cadence. For the seeded games (all `termMonths: 1`)
166	  // and any new Monthly/Annual order this is identical to the standard path.
167	  const months = isGame ? Math.max(1, Math.round(server.termMonths)) : vpsTerm(server.termMonths).months;
168	  // The annual discount to price the term at: the rate FROZEN on the server at sale,
169	  // falling back to the live setting for legacy/monthly rows. Both halves resolve
170	  // the same number, so an annual sub renews at the sold rate.
171	  const annualPct = server.annualDiscountPct ?? prices.annualDiscountPct;
172	  // Extra root disk is billed EVERY cycle at the current per-GB price. Game plans
173	  // are a flat all-in price and never carry the add-on lines.
174	  const extraDiskMonthlyCents = isGame ? 0 : extraDiskCentsAt(server.extraDiskGB, prices.extraDiskPerGbCents);
175	  const extraDiskCents = extraDiskMonthlyCents * months;
176	  // Paid backup retention (Plus) rides alongside extra disk: billed every cycle at
177	  // the current admin price, and — like every add-on line — NOT carried by a game
178	  // plan (renewalCharge's game branch is flat all-in, so game servers are never
179	  // sold a paid backup tier; see lib/backup-upgrade.ts's game guard).
180	  const backupMonthlyCents = isGame ? 0 : backupTierMonthlyCents(server.backupTier, prices.backupPlusCents);
181	  const backupCents = backupMonthlyCents * months;
182	  // GRANDFATHER PROGRAM: the frozen rate wins over the live catalog price when
183	  // set (see PricedServer.grandfatheredRenewalCents's own doc comment) — this
184	  // is the ONE substitution point for both branches below, so a price rise on
185	  // the live Plan/GamePlan row never touches a server that already has a
186	  // frozen rate, while every other renewal-formula behavior (term math, annual
187	  // discount, add-ons) is completely unchanged.
188	  const grandfatheredPriceCents = server.grandfatheredRenewalCents ?? null;
189	  // A game plan's `priceCents` is its MONTHLY base (every seed is `termMonths: 1`).
190	  // Divide by the plan's own term so an admin plan configured as, say, a 3-month
191	  // bundle still yields a per-month rate; then price the customer's chosen term
192	  // through the SAME formula VPS uses. For a monthly game server this is exactly
193	  // `priceCents`; an ANNUAL game server renews at 12× that, less the annual discount.
194	  const gameMonthlyCents = isGame
195	    ? Math.round((grandfatheredPriceCents ?? server.gamePlan!.priceCents) / Math.max(1, server.gamePlan!.termMonths))
196	    : 0;
197	  // LEGACY GUARD. Game servers sold BEFORE terms existed carry no frozen annual rate
198	  // (`annualDiscountPct == null`) and always renewed at the plan's FLAT `priceCents`,
199	  // with no term discount ever applied. Preserve that exactly so no pre-existing game
200	  // server's renewal moves — only servers sold through the new term-aware flow (which
201	  // always stamps a frozen `annualDiscountPct`) are priced with `termPriceCents`.
202	  //
203	  // GUARD ON isGame FIRST. This value is only USED in the isGame branch below, but a
204	  // bare ternary evaluates it for EVERY server — and a VPS `PricedServer` (e.g. the one
205	  // the deploy wizard builds, `gamePlan: null`, no `annualDiscountPct`) then hits the
206	  // `annualDiscountPct == null` arm and dereferences `server.gamePlan!.priceCents` on a
207	  // null, crashing the whole deploy page with "Cannot read properties of null". Compute
208	  // 0 for non-game so the null is never touched.
209	  const gameTotalCents = !isGame
210	    ? 0
211	    : server.annualDiscountPct == null
212	      ? (grandfatheredPriceCents ?? server.gamePlan!.priceCents)
213	      : termPriceCents(gameMonthlyCents, months, annualPct);
214	  // Bill the IP surcharge only when the server BOTH actually holds a dedicated
215	  // IP AND the customer chose/paid for it (`wantsDedicatedIp`). Requiring
216	  // `dedicatedIp` alone used to mean two very different bugs at different times:
217	  // a NAT-fallback server (paid for an IP, pool was empty, never got one) being
218	  // charged for an IP it never received, and — found 2026-09-15 via a real
219	  // customer's admin profile showing a $2.99 "committed MRR" they never agreed
220	  // to — the opposite case: a VPS granted a dedicated IP for FREE by the
221	  // `dedicated_ip_default` platform setting (see worker/index.ts's provision())
222	  // being silently billed for it anyway on the next renewal. Requiring BOTH
223	  // flags fixes both directions: no charge without the address, no charge
224	  // without genuine customer intent to pay for it.
225	  const dedicatedIpBillable = !!server.dedicatedIp && server.wantsDedicatedIp;
226	  const preRetentionNetCents = isGame
227	    ? gameTotalCents + (dedicatedIpBillable ? prices.ipMonthlyCents * months : 0)
228	    : vpsTermPriceCents(grandfatheredPriceCents ?? server.plan.priceCents, months, annualPct) +
229	      (dedicatedIpBillable ? prices.ipMonthlyCents * months : 0) +
230	      extraDiskCents +
231	      backupCents;
232	  // RETENTION OFFER: a one-time percent-off THIS renewal only (see
233	  // PricedServer.pendingRenewalDiscountPercent's own doc comment). Applied to
234	  // the WHOLE pre-tax subtotal — plan plus every add-on line — because "50% off
235	  // your next renewal" is a single-event promise about the bill, not about one
236	  // line on it. Clamped 0..100 so a corrupt/out-of-range stored value can never
237	  // produce a negative charge or mint a discount beyond what was ever written
238	  // (claimRetentionOffer only ever writes 50). Applied BEFORE tax, matching
239	  // every other discount on this platform (coupons, promos) — the customer is
240	  // taxed on what they actually pay, not on the list price.
241	  const pendingDiscountPercent = Math.max(0, Math.min(100, server.pendingRenewalDiscountPercent ?? 0));
242	  const retentionDiscountCents =
243	    pendingDiscountPercent > 0 ? Math.round((preRetentionNetCents * pendingDiscountPercent) / 100) : 0;
244	  const netCents = preRetentionNetCents - retentionDiscountCents;
245	  // VAT/GST on the pre-tax subtotal. Default rate 0 keeps `totalCents === netCents`
246	  // for every caller that does not pass the owner's rate (Finding 1).
247	  const taxRatePercent =
248	    Number.isFinite(prices.taxRatePercent) && (prices.taxRatePercent ?? 0) > 0 ? prices.taxRatePercent! : 0;
249	  const taxCents = Math.round((netCents * taxRatePercent) / 100);
250	  return {
251	    months,
252	    netCents,
253	    taxCents,
254	    taxRatePercent,
255	    totalCents: netCents + taxCents,
256	    extraDiskCents,
257	    extraDiskMonthlyCents,
258	    backupCents,
259	    backupMonthlyCents,
260	    retentionDiscountCents,
261	    label: isGame ? server.gamePlan!.name : `${server.plan.name} VPS`,
262	  };
263	}

200	export function orderPriceOf(
201	  quote: {
202	    chargeCents: number;
203	    promo: { discountPercent: number; name: string };
204	  },
205	  tax?: { taxCents: number; ratePercent: number; country: string } | null,
206	): OrderPrice {
207	  return {
208	    chargeCents: quote.chargeCents,
209	    promoPercent: quote.promo.discountPercent,
210	    promoName: quote.promo.name,
211	    ...(tax
212	      ? { taxCents: tax.taxCents, taxRatePercent: tax.ratePercent, taxCountry: tax.country }
213	      : {}),
214	  };
215	}

217	/**
218	 * Parse a sold price back off Stripe metadata. Returns null unless EVERY field is
219	 * well-formed: a half-parsed price would be worse than no price at all, because
220	 * the caller's fallback (re-quote) is at least internally consistent.
221	 */
222	export function parseOrderPrice(raw: unknown): OrderPrice | null {
223	  let obj: unknown = raw;
224	  if (typeof raw === "string") {
225	    try {
226	      obj = JSON.parse(raw);
227	    } catch {
228	      return null;
229	    }
230	  }
231	  if (!obj || typeof obj !== "object") return null;
232	  const { chargeCents, promoPercent, promoName, taxCents, taxRatePercent, taxCountry } =
233	    obj as Record<string, unknown>;
234	  if (typeof chargeCents !== "number" || !Number.isInteger(chargeCents) || chargeCents < 0) return null;
235	  if (typeof promoPercent !== "number" || !Number.isInteger(promoPercent)) return null;
236	  if (promoPercent < 0 || promoPercent > 100) return null;
237	  // Tax fields are ADDITIVE and lenient: a session written before Finding 1 (or with a
238	  // malformed tax field) carries none, and the charge path recomputes tax from the
239	  // owner's country — which undertaxes at worst, never overcharges.
240	  const tc = typeof taxCents === "number" && Number.isInteger(taxCents) && taxCents >= 0 ? taxCents : 0;
241	  const tr =
242	    typeof taxRatePercent === "number" && Number.isFinite(taxRatePercent) && taxRatePercent >= 0
243	      ? taxRatePercent
244	      : 0;
245	  return {
246	    chargeCents,
247	    promoPercent,
248	    promoName: typeof promoName === "string" ? promoName : "",
249	    taxCents: tc,
250	    taxRatePercent: tr,
251	    taxCountry: typeof taxCountry === "string" ? taxCountry : "",
252	  };
253	}

255	/** Extract a plain OrderIntent from a deploy form. */
256	export function intentFromFormData(formData: FormData): OrderIntent {
257	  return {
258	    planId: String(formData.get("planId") ?? ""),
259	    osTemplateId: String(formData.get("osTemplateId") ?? ""),
260	    hostname: String(formData.get("hostname") ?? ""),
261	    nodeId: String(formData.get("nodeId") ?? "") || undefined,
262	    region: String(formData.get("region") ?? "") || undefined,
263	    provider: (String(formData.get("provider") ?? "") || undefined) as OrderIntent["provider"],
264	    addonMalware: formData.get("addon_malware") === "1",
265	    addonBackup: formData.get("addon_backup") === "1",
266	    addonDocker: formData.get("addon_docker") === "1",
267	    termMonths: Number(formData.get("termMonths") ?? 1),
268	    dedicatedIp: formData.get("dedicatedIp") === "1",
269	    sshPublicKey: String(formData.get("sshPublicKey") ?? "").trim() || undefined,
270	    sshKeyName: String(formData.get("sshKeyName") ?? "deploy-key").slice(0, 60),
271	    free: formData.get("free") === "1",
272	    // Rounded DOWN to a purchasable step — a malformed value can only ever cost
273	    // the customer less, never more. Left UNDEFINED (not 0) when nothing was
274	    // bought so it drops out of JSON.stringify: the intent is round-tripped
275	    // through Stripe metadata, which is capped at 500 chars (lib/stripe.ts
276	    // createOrderCheckout), and every byte of headroom matters there.
277	    extraDiskGB: normalizeExtraDiskGB(formData.get("extraDiskGB")) || undefined,
278	    couponCode: String(formData.get("couponCode") ?? "").trim().toUpperCase() || undefined,
279	    // Only PLUS is a paid choice; left UNDEFINED for FREE (the included tier) so it
280	    // drops out of the Stripe-metadata JSON round-trip, like extraDiskGB. orderQuote
281	    // re-normalizes undefined back to FREE.

283	  };

286	/**
287	 * Pick the least-committed enabled node (RAM headroom), while steering AWAY from
288	 * a node this order would push to/past the CRITICAL capacity threshold when
289	 * another node has room. Falls back to primary (any node) when every candidate is
290	 * already critical — the scheduler never REFUSES an order for a capacity warning
291	 * (that's the node-capacity alert's job, lib/node-capacity.ts); it only prefers a
292	 * roomier node when one exists. DB-only so order placement never blocks on a
293	 * Proxmox round trip.
294	 */
295	/** Validate + price an order without placing it. Throws OrderError on any problem. */
296	export async function orderQuote(intent: OrderIntent, opts?: { suppressPromo?: boolean }) {
297	  const parsed = orderSchema.safeParse(intent);
298	  if (!parsed.success) throw new OrderError(parsed.error.issues[0]?.message ?? "Invalid input.");
299	  const plan = await db.plan.findUnique({ where: { id: intent.planId } });
300	  const os = await db.osTemplate.findUnique({ where: { id: intent.osTemplateId } });
301	  // A ONE-OFF CUSTOM plan (lib/custom-plan.ts createCustomPlan, "build a custom
302	  // server") is deliberately created `active: false` — every plain
303	  // `where: { active: true }` catalog/resize-picker/marketing query in this
304	  // codebase (30+ call sites, none scoped to a single order or customer) must
305	  // never surface it as a generically pickable tile. But it must still be a
306	  // valid target for the ONE order that just built it, so `sortOrder` — the
307	  // existing marker reserved for exactly this row shape — is accepted here as an
308	  // alternative to `active`. No other code path needs this carve-out: renewals
309	  // (lib/renewal-charge.ts) never check `active` at all, and the resize-target
310	  // picker's own `where: { active: true }` query correctly keeps a custom plan
311	  // out of every OTHER customer's upgrade options with no change needed there.
312	  const planPurchasable = !!plan?.active || plan?.sortOrder === CUSTOM_PLAN_SORT_ORDER;
313	  if (!planPurchasable || !os?.active) throw new OrderError("Plan or OS not available.");
314	  if (plan.ramMB < os.minRamMB || plan.diskGB < os.minDiskGB) {
315	    throw new OrderError(
316	      `${os.name} needs at least ${os.minRamMB / 1024} GB RAM and ${os.minDiskGB} GB disk — choose a larger plan.`,
317	    );
318	  }
319	  const term = vpsTerm(Number(intent.termMonths ?? 1));
320	  // The admin-configured ANNUAL discount, resolved ONCE here and passed to
321	  // `vpsTermPriceCents` so the annual term is charged at the same rate the deploy
322	  // wizard displayed and every renewal will bill. Ignored for non-annual terms.
323	  const annualPct = await annualDiscountPct();
324	  const ipCents = intent.dedicatedIp ? (await dedicatedIpMonthlyCents()) * term.months : 0;
325	
326	  // Extra root disk, priced per GB/month and multiplied over the term exactly
327	  // like the dedicated-IP add-on (and, like it, NOT discounted by the term or the
328	  // promo — the customer pays the same $/GB whichever term they pick, and renews
329	  // at the same rate). Growth is one-way: this is permanent for the server.
330	  const extraDiskGB = normalizeExtraDiskGB(intent.extraDiskGB);
331	  const extraDiskPerGb = extraDiskGB > 0 ? await extraDiskPerGbCents() : 0;
332	  const extraDiskMonthlyCents = extraDiskCentsAt(extraDiskGB, extraDiskPerGb);
333	  const extraDiskCents = extraDiskMonthlyCents * term.months;
334	  if (effectiveDiskGB(plan.diskGB, extraDiskGB) > EXTRA_DISK_MAX_TOTAL_GB) {
335	    throw new OrderError(`A server's disk tops out at ${EXTRA_DISK_MAX_TOTAL_GB} GB.`);
336	  }
337	
338	  // Paid backup RETENTION tier, priced per month and multiplied over the term
339	  // exactly like the extra-disk add-on (NOT promo-discounted — the customer pays
340	  // the same $/mo whichever term or promo, and renews at the same rate through
341	  // renewalCharge). Only PLUS is paid; FREE (the included tier) is $0.
342	  const backupTier = normalizeBackupTier(intent.backupTier);
343	  const backupMonthlyCents =
344	    backupTier === "FREE" ? 0 : backupTierMonthlyCents(backupTier, await backupPlusMonthlyCents());
345	  const backupCents = backupMonthlyCents * term.months;
346	
347	  // Seasonal promo = HONEST intro discount on the plan's FIRST-term charge only.
348	  // The regular term price (vpsTermPriceCents) is what renewals bill unchanged in
349	  // worker/billing.ts — so the strikethrough shown on the marketing pages is the
350	  // real renewal price and this discounted value is the real first-term price.
351	  // Marketing displays promoPriceCents(regular) too, so displayed === charged.
352	  // (Dedicated IP is billed at full price; the promo only touches the plan.)
353	  const regularPlanCents = vpsTermPriceCents(plan.priceCents, term.months, annualPct);
354	
355	  // LOW intro price → RENEWS at regular. A per-plan `introPriceCents` (set by an
356	  // admin) makes the FIRST term cheaper and leaves every renewal at the regular
357	  // `priceCents` — renewal code never reads the intro column, so renewal === regular
358	  // by construction (lib/renewal-charge.ts). Modelled as a first-term REDUCTION of
359	  // the regular term total (not a second price), so the regular term stays the one
360	  // basis renewals bill and proration prices against. `introDiscountCents` is 0 for
361	  // every plan without an intro price, so the whole VPS flow below is unchanged for
362	  // them. VPS never carries the first-month-free promo (`firstMonthFreeAppliesTo`),
363	  // so intro and FMF never stack here.
364	  const introMonthlyCents = planIntroMonthlyCents(plan);
365	  const introTermMonths = planIntroTermMonths(plan);
366	  const introDiscountCents = introFirstTermDiscountCents(
367	    plan.priceCents,
368	    introMonthlyCents,
369	    term.months,
370	    introTermMonths,
371	    annualPct,
372	  );
373	  // The plan-portion cash the FIRST term is sold at, intro applied. Renewals ignore it.
374	  const introFirstTermPlanCents = Math.max(0, regularPlanCents - introDiscountCents);
375	  // The rate this first term is sold at (percent off the regular term total) — stamped
376	  // on Server.termPromoPercent below via the promo object so proration/refunds price
377	  // against it exactly like a seasonal promo.
378	  const introPercent = introSoldPercent(regularPlanCents, introDiscountCents);
379	  const introRenewalMonthly = plan.priceCents; // what the "then $X/mo" copy quotes
380	  // When a plan has an intro price we present it THROUGH the same `promo` channel the
381	  // seasonal-sale plumbing uses (name + percent travel on OrderPrice and stamp
382	  // termPromoPercent). `firstMonthFree: false` keeps it out of the one-month-free
383	  // redemption machinery — an intro price has no per-account cap; it is simply this
384	  // plan's first-term price.
385	  const promo =
386	    introDiscountCents > 0
387	      ? {
388	          id: "intro-price",
389	          name: `Intro price — renews at $${(introRenewalMonthly / 100).toFixed(2)}/mo`,
390	          label: "Intro price",
391	          discountPercent: introPercent,
392	          firstMonthFree: false,
393	        }
394	      : currentPromo(new Date());
395	  // The promo is now MANAGED: the owner can switch it off, and every claim is
396	  // capped 1/account + 1/IP (lib/promo-redemption.ts). When the toggle is off the
397	  // quote shows — and placeOrder charges — the full price, so display === charged
398	  // on the disabled path. When it is on, the quote shows the first-month-free
399	  // price and the atomic claim in placeOrder's tx is the final arbiter of whether
400	  // the credit is actually granted (a lost race there is charged full).
401	  // `suppressPromo` prices this quote at FULL price even when the promo is on —
402	  // the card path uses it to re-quote for a customer who has already redeemed
403	  // (per-account/IP), so their Stripe leg and stamped total are full, not free.
404	  // The first-month-free promo is scoped to Shared Web Hosting only — VPS always
405	  // bills full. `firstMonthFreeAppliesTo("VPS")` is false, so promoEnabled is
406	  // false here and planFirstTermCents falls through to the regular term total.
407	  const promoEnabled =
408	    firstMonthFreeAppliesTo("VPS") && !opts?.suppressPromo && (await firstMonthFreeEnabled());
409	  // First-month-free must credit exactly ONE MONTH — not zero a multi-month term.
410	  // A naive promoPriceCents(termTotal) at 100% off would give a 36-month term 3
411	  // YEARS free. So we subtract one month of the plan's rate from the term total.
412	  // For a 1-month term this lands at $0 (genuinely first month free); for a 12/24/
413	  // 36-month term the customer pays the term minus one month. Renewals bill the
414	  // full vpsTermPriceCents unchanged (worker/billing.ts) — displayed === charged.
415	  const planFirstTermCents =
416	    promoEnabled && promo.firstMonthFree
417	      ? Math.max(0, regularPlanCents - plan.priceCents)
418	      : regularPlanCents;
419	  // The one-month credit this order gets IF the atomic claim succeeds. 0 when the
420	  // promo is off. placeOrder adds it back to charge full when the claim is lost.
421	  const promoCreditCents = regularPlanCents - planFirstTermCents;
422	
423	  // Optional checkout coupon: a service-locked, term-capped discount on the PLAN
424	  // portion only (not the dedicated-IP or extra-disk add-ons). Never throws for a
425	  // bad code — an invalid coupon leaves the price at full and surfaces `couponError`
426	  // so the deploy preview can show it; the redemption itself (count + per-user +
427	  // per-IP guards) is claimed atomically in placeOrder.
428	  let couponId: string | null = null;
429	  let couponDiscountCents = 0;
430	  let couponLabel = "";
431	  let couponError = "";
432	  let couponMaxRedemptions: number | null = null;
433	  let couponFirstTimeOnly = false;
434	  let couponExcludeActiveCustomers = false;
435	  let couponTrialDays: number | null = null;
436	  const code = (intent.couponCode ?? "").trim().toUpperCase();
437	  if (code) {
438	    if (!(await getSettingBool("coupons_enabled", true))) {
439	      couponError = "Promo codes are currently disabled.";
440	    } else {
441	      const coupon = await db.coupon.findUnique({ where: { code } });
442	      if (!coupon) {
443	        couponError = "That code isn’t valid.";
444	      } else {
445	        const verdict = couponOrderDiscountCents(
446	          {
447	            kind: coupon.kind,
448	            value: coupon.value,
449	            serviceKind: coupon.serviceKind,
450	            planSlug: coupon.planSlug,
451	            maxTermMonths: coupon.maxTermMonths,
452	            active: coupon.active,
453	            expiresAt: coupon.expiresAt,
454	            maxRedemptions: coupon.maxRedemptions,
455	            timesRedeemed: coupon.timesRedeemed,
456	            minAmountCents: coupon.minAmountCents,
457	          },
458	          {
459	            serviceKind: "VPS",
460	            planSlug: plan.slug,
461	            planMonthlyCents: plan.priceCents,
462	            termMonths: term.months,
463	            // Coupon discounts the intro-reduced plan portion, so an intro price and a
464	            // coupon cannot together drive the plan charge below zero, and a percentage
465	            // coupon is honestly "% off what you actually pay this term".
466	            planChargeCents: introFirstTermPlanCents,
467	          },
468	          new Date(),
469	        );
470	        if (verdict.ok) {
471	          couponId = coupon.id;
472	          couponDiscountCents = verdict.discountCents;
473	          couponLabel = verdict.label;
474	          couponMaxRedemptions = coupon.maxRedemptions;
475	          couponFirstTimeOnly = coupon.firstTimeOnly;
476	          couponExcludeActiveCustomers = coupon.excludeActiveCustomers;
477	          couponTrialDays = coupon.trialDays;
478	        } else {
479	          couponError = verdict.error;
480	        }
481	      }
482	    }
483	  }
484	
485	  const chargeCents = introFirstTermPlanCents - couponDiscountCents + ipCents + extraDiskCents + backupCents;
486	  // What THIS order actually renews at, every cycle, forever — the number the
487	  // wizard's "Then $X every {term}" caption must show. Renewals never carry a
488	  // coupon or an intro discount (both are strictly first-term-only — see
489	  // introRenewalMonthly's own comment and lib/renewal-charge.ts, the ONE
490	  // renewal formula every real charge uses), so this is `regularPlanCents`
491	  // (the term-priced plan, no discount) plus every recurring add-on line at
492	  // FULL price — the exact same sum renewalCharge() computes for the real
493	  // charge, just assembled from this function's own already-computed parts
494	  // instead of re-deriving it. Fixed live 2026-09-14: the wizard was instead
495	  // showing `introRenewalMonthly` (== bare plan.priceCents, meant only for
496	  // the narrower "intro price renews at $X/mo" caption on plans with an
497	  // admin intro rate) for EVERY order, so a server bought with Backup Plus
498	  // or a dedicated IP quoted a renewal price that silently excluded them —
499	  // correct on the invoice and the real recurring charge the whole time, just
500	  // wrong on the one screen a customer actually reads before paying.
501	  const renewalTotalCents = regularPlanCents + ipCents + extraDiskCents + backupCents;
502	  return {
503	    plan,
504	    os,
505	    term,
506	    chargeCents,
507	    // Intro pricing (0 / null on plans without one). `introDiscountCents` is the
508	    // first-term saving already baked into `chargeCents`; `introFirstTermPlanCents`
509	    // is the plan-portion cash the first term is sold at; the monthly figures drive
510	    // the honest "$intro first term, then $regular/mo" copy on the pricing cards.
511	    introDiscountCents,
512	    introFirstTermPlanCents,
513	    introMonthlyCents,
514	    introTermMonths,
515	    introRenewalMonthly,
516	    renewalTotalCents,
517	    introPercent,
518	    // The annual-discount rate this quote was priced at — snapshot onto the Server at
519	    // sale (Finding 2) so every later proration reads the SAME basis and a round trip
520	    // nets to zero even if the admin retunes `annual_discount_percent` in between.
521	    annualPct,
522	    promo,
523	    promoCreditCents,
524	    regularPlanCents,
525	    extraDiskGB,
526	    extraDiskMonthlyCents,
527	    extraDiskCents,
528	    backupTier,
529	    backupMonthlyCents,
530	    backupCents,
531	    ipCents,
532	    couponId,
533	    couponDiscountCents,
534	    couponLabel,
535	    couponError,

537	    couponFirstTimeOnly,
538	    couponExcludeActiveCustomers,
539	    couponTrialDays,
540	  };
541	}
542	
543	/**
544	 * Place an order: validate, charge the wallet (unless a free admin grant),
545	 * create the Server + PROVISION job. Returns the new server id. Does NOT
546	 * redirect. Callers must ensure funds exist (or pass free) — this still
547	 * enforces balance and throws OrderError("Insufficient balance.") otherwise.
548	 *
549	 * `sold` overrides the recomputed price with the one the order was actually SOLD
550	 * at — the card-paid path passes the figure stamped on the Checkout session
551	 * BEFORE the card was charged, so the confirm redirect settles the price the
552	 * customer consented to instead of re-pricing against whatever promo is running
553	 * when they get back (mirrors `chargeCents` in lib/resize.ts applyResize and
554	 * lib/disk-expand.ts applyDiskExpand). The wallet path omits it and pays the
555	 * quote, which it computed moments ago in the same request. See OrderPrice.
556	 */
557	/**
558	 * Claim a checkout coupon in ITS OWN atomic transaction, throwing OrderError on
559	 * any failure so nothing partial survives. Kept separate from the order tx so a
560	 * wallet order can surface the failure before any money moves, and a card order
561	 * (already paid) can swallow it without stranding the paid provision.
562	 *
563	 * Guards, all enforced here: first-time-only (no prior paid server), the
564	 * redemption cap (atomic conditional increment), one-per-account and one-per-IP
565	 * (the two @@unique constraints on CouponRedemption).
566	 */
567	export async function claimOrderCoupon(opts: {
568	  couponId: string;
569	  maxRedemptions: number | null;
570	  firstTimeOnly: boolean;
571	  /** See Coupon.excludeActiveCustomers's own doc comment — distinct from firstTimeOnly. */
572	  excludeActiveCustomers?: boolean;
573	  userId: string;
574	  ipHash: string | null;
575	  amountCents: number;
576	}): Promise<void> {
577	  await db.$transaction(async (tx) => {
578	    // Self-heal first: a dead hold from THIS customer's own abandoned card checkout must
579	    // not stand between them and this coupon on a fresh (wallet) order — and its global
580	    // slot is handed back here too. Guarded to expired RESERVED rows (lib/coupon-redemption.ts).
581	    await releaseExpiredCouponHoldsFor(tx, opts.couponId, opts.userId, opts.ipHash);
582	    if (opts.firstTimeOnly) {
583	      const prior = await tx.server.count({ where: { userId: opts.userId, isFree: false } });
584	      if (prior > 0) throw new OrderError("This code is for first-time customers only.");
585	    }
586	    if (opts.excludeActiveCustomers) {
587	      const active = await tx.server.count({
588	        where: { userId: opts.userId, isFree: false, status: { not: "DELETING" } },
589	      });
590	      if (active > 0) throw new OrderError("This offer is for accounts with no active service.");
591	    }
592	    // Atomic conditional increment — the only thing between the last free slot and
593	    // an over-redemption when two orders race for it.
594	    const claim = await tx.coupon.updateMany({
595	      where:
596	        opts.maxRedemptions === null
597	          ? { id: opts.couponId, active: true }
598	          : { id: opts.couponId, active: true, timesRedeemed: { lt: opts.maxRedemptions } },
599	      data: { timesRedeemed: { increment: 1 } },
600	    });
601	    if (claim.count !== 1) throw new OrderError("That code has just been fully claimed.");
602	    try {
603	      await tx.couponRedemption.create({
604	        data: { couponId: opts.couponId, userId: opts.userId, ipHash: opts.ipHash, amountCents: opts.amountCents, context: "order" },
605	      });
606	    } catch {
607	      // Unique violation on (coupon,user) or (coupon,ipHash): already claimed by
608	      // this person. Throwing rolls back the increment above with it.
609	      throw new OrderError("You’ve already used this code.");
610	    }
611	  });
612	}
613	
614	/**
615	 * Read-only mirror of `claimOrderCoupon`'s per-person guards, for the CARD path.
616	 *
617	 * The card leg discounts `cardCents` up front and only settles the redemption
618	 * AFTER the card is charged — where a failed claim is deliberately swallowed so a
619	 * paid provision is never stranded. Without this pre-check, a customer who has
620	 * already used a one-per-person code (or isn't first-time) still gets the
621	 * discounted card charge and the swallow hides it. So before we send them to
622	 * checkout we re-run first-time-only, one-per-account, one-per-IP and the cap as
623	 * plain reads; if any fails the caller re-quotes at full price. This is advisory
624	 * (a race could still lose the atomic claim at settle time — that path stays
625	 * swallowed by design), but it closes the everyday bypass.
626	 */
627	export async function orderCouponClaimable(opts: {
628	  couponId: string;
629	  firstTimeOnly: boolean;
630	  /** See Coupon.excludeActiveCustomers's own doc comment — distinct from firstTimeOnly. */
631	  excludeActiveCustomers?: boolean;
632	  maxRedemptions: number | null;
633	  userId: string;
634	  ipHash: string | null;
635	}): Promise<{ ok: true } | { ok: false; error: string }> {
636	  if (opts.firstTimeOnly) {
637	    const prior = await db.server.count({ where: { userId: opts.userId, isFree: false } });
638	    if (prior > 0) return { ok: false, error: "This code is for first-time customers only." };
639	  }
640	  if (opts.excludeActiveCustomers) {
641	    const active = await db.server.count({
642	      where: { userId: opts.userId, isFree: false, status: { not: "DELETING" } },
643	    });
644	    if (active > 0) return { ok: false, error: "This offer is for accounts with no active service." };
645	  }
646	  const byUser = await db.couponRedemption.findUnique({
647	    where: { couponId_userId: { couponId: opts.couponId, userId: opts.userId } },
648	  });
649	  if (byUser) return { ok: false, error: "You’ve already used this code." };
650	  if (opts.ipHash) {
651	    const byIp = await db.couponRedemption.findFirst({ where: { couponId: opts.couponId, ipHash: opts.ipHash } });
652	    if (byIp) return { ok: false, error: "This code has already been claimed from your connection." };
653	  }
654	  if (opts.maxRedemptions !== null) {
655	    const c = await db.coupon.findUnique({ where: { id: opts.couponId }, select: { timesRedeemed: true, active: true } });
656	    if (!c || !c.active || c.timesRedeemed >= opts.maxRedemptions) return { ok: false, error: "This code has reached its redemption limit." };
657	  }
658	  return { ok: true };
659	}

Now I need to add a new partner discount layer (50% off first purchase, 10% recurring) that composes correctly with all of this across VPS, game servers, cloud hosting, and business email orders.

I need to determine "first purchase" status by checking whether the customer has any prior paid invoice for a real, non-domain, non-topup purchase, similar to the existing first-time-coupon pattern, but extended to cover all service types since the discount applies to any purchase except domains.

I'll apply this discount logic in the VPS quote, game order quote, and cloud/email quote paths, while domains remain excluded entirely from the discount.

For the "must be visible before first purchase" requirement, marketing pricing pages need to detect a partner attachment or valid cookie before checkout even happens, server-side, for anonymous visitors — checking the referral cookie against valid partner codes and distinguishing logged-in attached customers from anonymous cookie-only visitors.

Since attachment only happens at registration, anonymous visitors with a valid cookie would see a "get 50% off your first purchase" preview banner rather than an already-discounted price, while logged-in attached customers get the actual 50% or 10% reflected depending on whether it's their first purchase.

On checkout/order wizard pages, users are typically already logged in, so I can just show the real discounted unit price there. For anonymous marketing pages, since this is Next.js with dynamic rendering enabled elsewhere, I can still read cookies server-side to decide whether to show the promotional banner, even before registration.

I'll build a shared helper that returns the partner discount status for a user or cookie code, then wire it into the order quote logic so the charged price reflects it. I need to be careful that the dedicated-IP exclusion only applies to commission calculations, not to what the customer actually pays — the customer's discount should apply on top of whatever price they'd already get from other promos.

On the customer side, the discount applies to the full charge (including IP, disk, backup addons) for VPS and game orders, but excludes domain purchases entirely — that's a separate rule from the commission exclusion.

I notice the partner dashboard page already exists with a fairly complete UI, separate from the peer referral page. I need to extend it with click/signup/conversion analytics, a media kit, terms, the referral code and link, and a fuller payout history beyond just the commissions list.

For the partial settlement requirement, I realize marking an arbitrary dollar amount as paid doesn't cleanly map to flipping specific commission rows to PAID status, so I need a new model to track payout events distinctly from individual commission records. I'm designing a PartnerPayout model to record these settlement events with their own amount and date, linked back to the partner.

But this creates a tricky balance calculation problem: if a partial payout happens while ACCRUED commission rows stay ACCRUED, then a later full settlement could double-count the amount already paid through the separate payout record. I need to rethink how outstanding balance gets computed so these two mechanisms don't conflict.

Actually, matching this codebase's ledger-simplicity philosophy, I don't need per-invoice precision here — admins just want to log a payment event and see the balance update. So I'll add PartnerPayout as a simple record of actual payments (any amount, partial or full), keep PartnerCommission.status for audit history, but compute outstanding balance as total accrued minus total payouts, clamped at zero.

I realize flipping ACCRUED rows to PAID is now purely cosmetic since outstanding is derived from payouts, but leaving row status stale would create inconsistency, so the pragmatic path is to add a PartnerPayout model with amount, note, and timestamp, and keep it simple given the light requirement of just marking an amount as paid off the balance.

For the summary computation, outstanding becomes the lifetime accrued (non-void) commissions minus the sum of payouts, floored at zero. The existing full-settle function will use this new formula, create a single "Full settlement" payout for the outstanding amount, and still flip all ACCRUED rows to PAID so the per-row ledger display stays consistent for that common case.

A new `adminRecordPartnerPayout` function will validate the amount is positive and doesn't exceed outstanding, then simply record a payout row without trying to flip individual commission rows — that's too fiddly on partial payments. Instead, the commission status badges become secondary display info, while the true running balance is always the accrued-minus-paid calculation, mirroring a clean two-ledger accounting approach (earned vs. paid).

For backward compatibility, I'll still flip a commission row to PAID when a payout exactly matches the full outstanding amount, but partial payouts leave rows as ACCRUED while correctly reducing the aggregate outstanding total. I need to update the ledger UI so the top-line Accrued/Paid/Outstanding figures reflect this properly.

I'll add a Payout History table listing PartnerPayout records as the authoritative payment log the owner wants, which is a reasonable design given constraints, so I'll move to writing the code. Next I should think through the click tracking schema — since click volume can be high, I need to check whether per-click rows or aggregated counters fit existing patterns, looking at how other high-volume events like Visit/analytics tables are handled.

668	 * second worker or a concurrent `renewNow` all read the same snapshot expiry; only

671	 * renewed this period, which is a success for us, not an error.
672	 */

content.thinking:
I'm mapping out the many call sites across actions, payment providers, Stripe webhook fulfilment, and the quote wizard that would need consistent updates if I change this signature—which is a fair amount of risk to weigh before proceeding.

Looking closer at the webhook, it falls back to a fresh `orderQuote` call when `sold` isn't available, so I should pass userId there too if it's in scope. Similarly `lib/actions-payment-providers.ts` handles the card/PayPal path and stamps the sold price onto the checkout session, so it also needs the userId to keep the quoted amount consistent with what gets charged later.

Given time constraints, rather than building a full reservation-token system to atomically claim the partner first-purchase discount flag (mirroring the promo/coupon hold-and-confirm machinery), I'll go with a simpler safe approach: attempt an atomic claim of `firstPurchaseDiscountUsedAt` inside the existing wallet-debit transactions in `placeOrder` and `placeGameOrder`, setting it only if still null at that point.

For the WALLET path, since there's no time gap between quote and transaction, if the claim succeeds the 50% rate holds; if it fails (already claimed), I recompute the higher fallback rate and charge that instead, similar to how `soldFull` is handled. For the CARD path, since Stripe charges externally based on a quote stamped ahead of time and can't be adjusted post-hoc if the race is lost, fulfilment just calls `placeOrder` with the already-decided `sold.chargeCents` verbatim.

If a rare double-claim race occurs on the card path (same customer, two concurrent first-time orders), the second one would already be charged the discounted amount via Stripe by the time fulfilment runs and the atomic claim fails — mirroring the existing promo/coupon "swallow" pattern in the codebase, where a lost race after a card charge just gets logged and the discounted sold price is kept rather than trying to recharge.

Now I'm defining the partner discount module: a read-only type describing whether a customer is attached to an active partner, their discount tier, and first-purchase eligibility, plus a function that resolves this info purely for display/quoting without claiming anything.

I'm adding a helper to resolve discount preview from a raw referral code, used for marketing pages or anonymous visitors with a referral cookie but no account — showing the 50% first-purchase preview since they have no purchase history. Then I'm writing the atomic claim function itself, meant to be called only inside the charge transaction, which returns the actual percent this specific charge is allowed to use based on claim state.

Actually, I'm reconsidering the approach — rather than a claim model requiring compare-and-swap logic duplicated across multiple order paths (VPS, game, wallet, card combinations), I'm leaning toward a simpler race-safe design where the discount tier gets computed from whether `firstPurchaseDiscountUsedAt` is still null at quote time.

But then inside the actual charge transaction, right where the wallet debit happens, I'd need to perform that same atomic claim update, only when the percent was the first-purchase tier — and if that update matches zero rows, meaning a concurrent order already consumed the slot, I'd have discovered the race too late for the wallet path, since recomputing at the lower rate would require rebuilding the invoice line with a different charge amount than what was already computed before the transaction started.

That would mean restructuring chunks of `placeOrder`/`placeGameOrder`, which is a lot of intrusive surgery into already extremely complex, carefully-commented money code — I should touch this minimally to avoid breaking the existing wallet promo/coupon logic interleaved there. Given how vanishingly rare this exact race actually is (same customer submitting two simultaneous first-ever-purchase orders), and how minor the harm would be either way, I'm leaning toward a pragmatic, honestly-documented simplification instead of a fully bulletproof fix.

I'm sketching this out: at quote time read `firstPurchaseDiscountUsedAt` to determine the discount tier, then attempt an atomic claim only when applying the 50% rate, using a conditional update that only succeeds if the flag is still null — mirroring the same "log and keep, don't recompute" discipline used elsewhere in this codebase for equally rare races like the vanishing coupon hold.

If the discount was already 10% at quote time or the order isn't attached to a partner at all, there's nothing to claim. I want to flag this explicitly as a deliberate, narrow tradeoff consistent with the codebase's existing swallow-discipline rather than overengineering for a rare race. So the claim needs to live inside both `placeOrder`'s and `placeGameOrder`'s transactions, and since the card/Stripe fulfillment path also calls `placeOrder`, that same claim logic covers it too.

I realize `placeOrder` still recomputes a fresh quote even on the card path, mostly using it for fields like plan, OS, term, and disk size rather than the charge amount itself — since that quote computation needs the userId to determine the partner discount, I can just pass `user.id` in when calling it from inside `placeOrder`.

But I also need to check the Stripe checkout session creation, since that's stamped with a price before the user pays — if I don't pass userId there too, a partner-discounted customer would see one price in the wizard but get charged full price at checkout. So I need to trace through `lib/stripe.ts`, `lib/actions-payment-providers.ts`, `lib/actions.ts`, and `lib/nx/quote.ts` to confirm userId is available at each call site and update them consistently so displayed and charged prices always match.

Given the scope — roughly 13 VPS call sites and 6 game call sites — I'll make `orderQuote` and `gameOrderQuote` accept an optional `userId` param, defaulting to undefined so nothing breaks, then work through updating every call site where a user/session exists to actually pass it through.

I'll handle the money-critical core myself carefully — the schema, discount logic in orderQuote/gameOrderQuote, renewal charges, the dedicated-ip commission exclusion, and the invoice line/claim logic in placeOrder/placeGameOrder — since precision matters most there, while treating the call-site threading as mostly mechanical edits I can move through quickly by checking each file's context first.

For the schema migration adding dedicated IP cents, first purchase discount tracking, partner payouts, and partner invites, I need to figure out whether my isolated worktree actually has its own database or shares one with the other worktrees, since CLAUDE.md warns against building against the shared environment directly.

# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.
- Admin impersonation: `impersonateUser()` sets a signed cookie; `currentUser()` returns the target, `realUser()` the actual admin; banner + exit handled in Shell. Admin pages call `realUser`/`requireAdmin` and refuse to render while impersonating.
- Metrics come from Proxmox RRD via `/api/metrics` (node for admins, per-server for owners). A server with no `vmid` yet is not "not found" — it's "not provisioned yet," and gets a `{data: [], unavailable: true}` 200 response, not a 404 (a 404 there caused a permanent client poll loop; same fix applied to `/api/servers/[id]/disk`).

## Working on this codebase — one tree, any session

`/opt/nxeon` (this directory, branch `main`) is the single source of truth. There is no longer a required separate sandbox for ordinary changes — the node-2 box (`/opt/nxeon-v2`) that incubated the Nexion redesign still exists and is safe to use for a large, risky, or highly iterative piece of work (it runs sandboxed: `NXEON_SANDBOX=1` stubs Proxmox provisioning and Stripe charges), but is optional, not a gate. Any session — this one or another — can edit `main` directly and ship through the pipeline below.

1. Edit, then `npx tsc --noEmit` before building anything.
2. `npm run build` locally only to catch build errors before pushing — do not restart production services from an ad hoc build in this directory (see Commands below); this is validation, not deployment.
3. Commit (small, real commits — the GitHub post-commit hook auto-pushes `origin`).
4. `scripts/deploy-staging.sh <ref>` — builds, migrates, and restarts staging (`:8080`) from that ref. **Actually look at what you changed there** (screenshot a UI change, click through a flow) before promoting — a change that typechecks and builds can still be visibly broken; this session's own audit caught a large batch of real bugs (broken light mode, frozen animations, missing form validation, wrong prices) that all passed typecheck cleanly.
5. `scripts/promote-production.sh` — rebuilds and restarts production from whatever `main` currently has checked out. It refuses to run if staging isn't healthy first.

If two sessions are likely to be editing at once, coordinate the ordinary way: pull before starting, small commits, push often (the auto-push hook does this for you on commit).

## Integrations (activate via /opt/nxeon/.env)

- **Stripe**: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` + `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` → wallet top-ups switch from demo gateway to Checkout (`/api/stripe/checkout`, webhook `/api/stripe/webhook`, event `checkout.session.completed`, idempotent by session id). Saved cards live in `PaymentCard` (added with the Nexion schema) — a customer who saved a card before that table existed has their card represented only by the older `User.stripeCustomerId`/`stripePaymentMethodId` columns; `hasChargeableCard`/renewals read those directly and are unaffected, but the Billing page's card list reads `PaymentCard`, so a pre-existing card needs the one-off backfill (`scripts/backfill-payment-cards.ts`) to show up there. That backfill has already been run once for every account with a legacy card as of 2026-09-14; it's idempotent, safe to re-run if a new gap appears.
- **Namecheap** (`lib/namecheap.ts`): `NAMECHEAP_API_USER/KEY/USERNAME/CLIENT_IP` (+`NAMECHEAP_SANDBOX=1` for testing) → domain search/register/renew/DNS management. TLD retail prices in `TLD_PRICES`.
- **GitHub**: remote `origin` = `git@github.com:santino1233/nxeon.git` via deploy key `/root/.ssh/nxeon_deploy`. Every commit auto-pushes via `.git/hooks/post-commit`. `.env`/credentials are gitignored — never commit secrets.

## Conventions

- All state changes to VMs go through `Job` rows — the web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly (read-only status calls are OK).
- One in-flight job per server (enforced in `serverAction`).
- Admin-only actions live in [lib/actions.ts](lib/actions.ts) and must call `requireAdmin()`.
- Free VPSes: `Server.isFree = true`, no billing, `expiresAt = null`.

227	    ? Math.round((grandfatheredPriceCents ?? server.gamePlan!.priceCents) / Math.max(1, server.gamePlan!.termMonths))
228	    : 0;
229	  // LEGACY GUARD. Game servers sold BEFORE terms existed carry no frozen annual rate
230	  // (`annualDiscountPct == null`) and always renewed at the plan's FLAT `priceCents`,
231	  // with no term discount ever applied. Preserve that exactly so no pre-existing game
232	  // server's renewal moves — only servers sold through the new term-aware flow (which
233	  // always stamps a frozen `annualDiscountPct`) are priced with `termPriceCents`.
234	  //
235	  // GUARD ON isGame FIRST. This value is only USED in the isGame branch below, but a
236	  // bare ternary evaluates it for EVERY server — and a VPS `PricedServer` (e.g. the one
237	  // the deploy wizard builds, `gamePlan: null`, no `annualDiscountPct`) then hits the
238	  // `annualDiscountPct == null` arm and dereferences `server.gamePlan!.priceCents` on a
239	  // null, crashing the whole deploy page with "Cannot read properties of null". Compute
240	  // 0 for non-game so the null is never touched.
241	  const gameTotalCents = !isGame
242	    ? 0
243	    : server.annualDiscountPct == null
244	      ? (grandfatheredPriceCents ?? server.gamePlan!.priceCents)
245	      : termPriceCents(gameMonthlyCents, months, annualPct);
246	  // Bill the IP surcharge only when the server BOTH actually holds a dedicated
247	  // IP AND the customer chose/paid for it (`wantsDedicatedIp`). Requiring
248	  // `dedicatedIp` alone used to mean two very different bugs at different times:
249	  // a NAT-fallback server (paid for an IP, pool was empty, never got one) being
250	  // charged for an IP it never received, and — found 2026-09-15 via a real
251	  // customer's admin profile showing a $2.99 "committed MRR" they never agreed
252	  // to — the opposite case: a VPS granted a dedicated IP for FREE by the
253	  // `dedicated_ip_default` platform setting (see worker/index.ts's provision())
254	  // being silently billed for it anyway on the next renewal. Requiring BOTH
255	  // flags fixes both directions: no charge without the address, no charge
256	  // without genuine customer intent to pay for it.
257	  const dedicatedIpBillable = !!server.dedicatedIp && server.wantsDedicatedIp;
258	  const preRetentionNetCents = isGame

13	 * WHY IT IS A WRAPPER RATHER THAN A FORMULA.
14	 *
15	 * The original incident: the button read `Renew now (+30 days, $8.99)` and
16	 * charged **$97.09**, moving the expiry twelve months — the label hardcoded
17	 * "+30 days" and the plan's MONTHLY price while `renewNow` charged a full term.
18	 * The fix was to compute the quote and the charge in one place.
19	 *
20	 * The second incident, hours later and in this very file: that shared place was
21	 * written as fresh arithmetic over `plan.priceCents`, which silently ignored
22	 * `gamePlan`. A game server carries BOTH a base `planId` and a `gamePlanId`, and
23	 * it is sold at the game plan's flat price — `minecraft-mm8w85` was sold at
24	 * $4.99 while its base Starter plan is $8.99. So the new shared quote would have
25	 * charged a game-server owner **80% more than they agreed to** the moment they

27	 * the automatic renewal sweep in `worker/billing.ts` already used it.
28	 *
29	 * The lesson is the one this codebase keeps relearning: the danger was never a
30	 * wrong formula, it was a SECOND formula. So there is exactly one, it lives in
31	 * `renewalCharge`, and everything that quotes or charges a renewal goes through
32	 * it — the worker sweep, the card path, this button, and the server page.
33	 */
