515	 * Place a game order: re-validate + price, capacity-check, then atomically debit
516	 * the wallet and create the Server (sized by the tier's base VPS plan, running the
517	 * game image, with the customer's variant + gameplay settings) plus a PROVISION
518	 * job. Returns the new server id. Does NOT redirect.
519	 *
520	 * `sold` (card path) overrides the recomputed price with the one the order was
521	 * SOLD at — the card-paid path passes the figure stamped on the Checkout session
522	 * BEFORE the card was charged, so the confirm/webhook fulfilment settles the price
523	 * the customer consented to instead of re-pricing against a rate that changed in
524	 * between. The wallet path omits it and pays the fresh quote it computed moments
525	 * ago. This mirrors `sold` in lib/order.ts placeOrder.
526	 *
527	 * Callers must ensure funds exist (the card leg pre-credits the wallet, the wallet
528	 * path is gated by the balance check in the action). This still enforces the
529	 * balance and throws GameOrderError("Insufficient balance…") otherwise — no overdraft.
530	 */
531	export async function placeGameOrder(
532	  user: User,
533	  intent: GameOrderIntent,
534	  sold?: GameOrderPrice | null,
535	  /** CARD path only: the hold `payAndDeployGame` reserved before the card was
536	   *  charged (see reserveOrderCoupon), confirmed here — RESERVED→CONSUMED —
537	   *  inside the same tx that commits the order. Mirrors lib/order.ts
538	   *  placeOrder's `opts.couponReservationToken` exactly. */
539	  couponReservationToken?: string | null,
540	): Promise<string> {
541	  const quote = await gameOrderQuote(intent);
542	
543	  // Resolve the ACTUAL hostname this server will get, now that the order is
544	  // really being placed (NOT inside gameOrderQuote, which the wizard calls on
545	  // every keystroke for a live price preview and has no business hitting the
546	  // DB or handing out a name it might never use). gameOrderQuote already
547	  // validated the format (or generated the "<family>-<rand>" default); this
548	  // only resolves UNIQUENESS, auto-suffixing on collision instead of letting
549	  // two customers' servers end up with the same hostname. See lib/hostname.ts.
550	  quote.hostname = await resolveUniqueHostname(quote.hostname, quote.gameFamily);
551	
552	  // CS2 needs a Steam Game Server Login Token to register with matchmaking at
553	  // all (SRCDS_TOKEN, no longer a required checkout field as of 2026-09-17 —
554	  // see lib/game-config.ts's field comment). Mint one automatically, ONCE,
555	  // here at actual order placement — never in gameOrderQuote, which the
556	  // wizard calls on every keystroke for a live price preview and would burn
557	  // through Valve's 1000-account-per-key budget on customers who never buy.
558	  // A customer who pasted their own token is left alone; a Steam API hiccup
559	  // degrades to "no token yet" (server still deploys and runs, just isn't
560	  // listed on matchmaking until one is added from the dashboard) rather than
561	  // failing the whole paid order over it.
562	  if (quote.gameFamily === "cs2" && !quote.values.SRCDS_TOKEN && steamGsltConfigured()) {
563	    try {
564	      const account = await createGameServerAccount(730, `nxeon:${quote.hostname}`);
565	      quote.values.SRCDS_TOKEN = account.loginToken;
566	      quote.values._SRCDS_TOKEN_STEAMID = account.steamid;
567	    } catch (e) {
568	      console.error(`[game-order] Steam GSLT auto-generation failed for ${quote.hostname}`, e);
569	    }
570	  }
571	
572	  // Bill off the SOLD price when present (never re-priced after the card cleared),
573	  // else the fresh quote (which already folds in any valid coupon discount) —
574	  // this scalar is the whole truth about what this order costs.
575	  const chargeCents = sold?.chargeCents ?? quote.chargeCents;
576	
577	  // Oversell guard — the VPS order path enforces this; game orders must too, or a
578	  // game server could commit host RAM past capacity.
579	  const capacity = await capacityCheck(quote.basePlanId);
580	  if (!capacity.ok) {
581	    throw new GameOrderError(capacity.reason ?? "The host is at capacity right now. Please try again shortly.");
582	  }
583	
584	  // Pick a node the same way a VPS order does — without this, every game
585	  // server's `nodeId` stays null and `worker/index.ts`'s `nodeFor()` fallback
586	  // (`server.node ?? primary node`) pins EVERY game server onto the primary
587	  // node forever, regardless of its actual load. Confirmed live: every game
588	  // server in production had nodeId: null and primary sat at 84% real RAM /
589	  // 200% committed CPU while other nodes were comparatively idle.
590	  //
591	  // Region-aware exactly like lib/order.ts placeOrder: a customer picks a
592	  // REGION, not a specific node, so it is resolved fresh here (least loaded
593	  // within that region) rather than trusting whatever node the wizard's
594	  // local preview happened to resolve at page-load time.
595	  const node = intent.region
596	    ? await scheduleNode(quote.ramMB, { region: intent.region, provider: intent.provider })
597	    : await scheduleNode(quote.ramMB);
598	  if (intent.region && !node) {
599	    throw new GameOrderError("That location is at capacity right now — please pick another.");
600	  }
601	
602	  // WALLET path: claim the coupon atomically BEFORE the balance gate/order tx,
603	  // so a wallet order fails cleanly (no money moved) if the code's last slot just
604	  // went, or this person already used it. Mirrors lib/order.ts placeOrder's own
605	  // wallet-path claim exactly (same shared claimOrderCoupon — one redemption
606	  // ledger for both VPS and game orders, not two).
607	  //
608	  // CARD path: does NOT claim here — `sold` means the card already charged the
609	  // discounted price, so a fresh claim now would double-count against the cap.
610	  // Real per-person enforcement for the card leg happens BEFORE the charge, via
611	  // `payAndDeployGame`'s reserveOrderCoupon hold (mirroring VPS's cardPromoToken);
612	  // this function only CONFIRMS that pre-existing hold below, inside the same tx
613	  // that commits the order — see confirmOrderCouponReservation's call site further
614	  // down. Added 2026-09-23 after a real gap: this path used to not gate the card
615	  // leg on any per-person limit at all, which the trial promo (a strictly
616	  // one-per-person, excludeActiveCustomers coupon) needed and didn't have.
617	  if (!sold && quote.couponId && quote.couponDiscountCents > 0) {
618	    try {
619	      await claimOrderCoupon({
620	        couponId: quote.couponId,
621	        maxRedemptions: quote.couponMaxRedemptions,
622	        firstTimeOnly: quote.couponFirstTimeOnly,
623	        excludeActiveCustomers: quote.couponExcludeActiveCustomers,
624	        userId: user.id,
625	        ipHash: null,
626	        amountCents: quote.couponDiscountCents,
627	      });
628	    } catch (e) {
629	      // claimOrderCoupon throws OrderError — translate to GameOrderError so
630	      // callers that only catch GameOrderError (payAndDeployGame, orderGameServer)

632	      // exception / generic error page.
633	      throw new GameOrderError(e instanceof Error ? e.message : "That code couldn't be applied.");
634	    }
635	  }
636	
637	  // Balance gate BEFORE the tx so we fail cleanly (no money moved). On the card
638	  // path the wallet was credited the card leg first, so this holds.
639	  if (user.balanceCents < chargeCents) {
640	    throw new GameOrderError("Insufficient balance. Top up your wallet first.");
641	  }
642	
643	  const effMonthly = quote.term > 1 ? Math.round(chargeCents / quote.term) : 0;
644	  const termLabel =
645	    quote.term > 1 ? `${vpsTerm(quote.term).label} ($${(effMonthly / 100).toFixed(2)}/mo)` : vpsTerm(quote.term).label;
646	
647	  // Line-item description shared by the wallet-transaction memo and the invoice —
648	  // mirrors lib/order.ts's VPS line ("<plan> VPS (<hostname>) — <term>"), the
649	  // pattern lib/actions-hosting.ts and lib/actions-email-hosting.ts also follow.
650	  const invDesc = `${quote.planName} Game Server (${quote.hostname}) — ${termLabel}`;
651	
652	  let server;
653	  // Captured from the in-tx invoice.create so the paid ORDER invoice can be emailed
654	  // (with its PDF) AFTER the transaction commits — a rolled-back order leaves this
655	  // null and emails nothing. Mirrors `orderInvoice` in lib/order.ts placeOrder.
656	  let orderInvoice: { id: string; number: number; amountCents: number } | null = null;
657	  try {
658	    server = await db.$transaction(async (tx) => {
659	      await debitWallet(tx, user.id, chargeCents);
660	      await tx.walletTransaction.create({
661	        data: {
662	          userId: user.id,
663	          amountCents: -chargeCents,
664	          description: `Game server: ${quote.planName} (${quote.gameFamily}) — ${termLabel}`,
665	        },
666	      });
667	      // Billing document for the charge — created inside the same debit tx so it
668	      // shares the transaction's atomicity (a rolled-back charge leaves no invoice),
669	      // exactly like lib/order.ts's VPS invoice and worker/billing.ts's renewal
670	      // invoice. Game has no VAT, and any coupon discount is already netted into
671	      // `chargeCents`, so this is still a single line for the (already net) charge.
672	      const createdInvoice = await tx.invoice.create({
673	        data: invoiceCreateData({
674	          userId: user.id,
675	          description: invDesc,
676	          status: "PAID",
677	          taxCents: 0,
678	          taxRatePercent: 0,
679	          taxCountry: null,
680	          // A trial coupon's invoice should say what it actually billed for —
681	          // 7 days, not a month it didn't charge for.
682	          period: {
683	            start: new Date(),
684	            end: quote.couponTrialDays ? addDays(new Date(), quote.couponTrialDays) : addMonths(new Date(), quote.term),
685	          },
686	          lineItems: [{ description: invDesc, qty: 1, unitCents: chargeCents, amountCents: chargeCents }],
687	        }),
688	      });
689	      orderInvoice = {
690	        id: createdInvoice.id,
691	        number: createdInvoice.number,
692	        amountCents: createdInvoice.amountCents,
693	      };
694	      // CARD/Stripe path: confirm the coupon hold reserved before the card was
695	      // charged (RESERVED→CONSUMED), inside this tx so the discount's slot
696	      // commits with the provision. NEVER a fresh claim — that would
697	      // re-increment the cap and collide on the per-person unique. `sold`

699	      // changes here. Mirrors lib/order.ts placeOrder's identical step.

718	          gamePlanId: quote.gamePlanId,
719	          osTemplateId: quote.osTemplateId,

736	          annualDiscountPct: quote.annualPct,

import { NextResponse } from "next/server";
import { checkRateLimit, clientIp, UNKNOWN_IP } from "@/lib/rate-limit";

/**
 * Trustworthy client-IP extraction for the public HTTP API.
 *
 * ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * THERE IS NO IMPLEMENTATION IN THIS FILE ANY MORE — AND THAT IS THE POINT
 * ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * `trustedClientIp` used to be a second, independent parser of the same headers
 * that `clientIp` in lib/rate-limit.ts already parsed. The two were written days
 * apart out of the same incident and each was better than the other at something:
 *
 *   lib/rate-limit.ts   had the TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS knob, so it stays correct if a
 *                       CDN is ever put in front of nginx — but it returned the
 *                       hop verbatim, valid address or not.
 *   this file           validated that the value was actually an IP and
 *                       normalised `::ffff:1.2.3.4` and `1.2.3.4:5678` to one
 *                       bucket — but hardcoded "one proxy".
 *
 * Both properties are now in the single `clientIp`, and this is an alias of it.
 * Keeping the name costs nothing (about fifteen route handlers import it) and
 * deleting the duplicate implementation removes the thing that actually hurts:
 * two answers to "who is calling", drifting apart, with no way for a reader to
 * know which one their call site should have used. A second definition of an
 * existing thing is this codebase's single most common defect class.
 *
 * ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUSTWORTHY (the incident, kept because it is load-bearing)
 * ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 * Every route in `app/api/**` used to carry a private copy of:
 *
 *     const xff = req.headers.get("x-forwarded-for") ?? "";
 *     return xff.split(",")[0]?.trim() || "unknown";     // ← FIRST hop
 *
 * with the comment "first hop of x-forwarded-for is the real client (nginx
 * appends downstream)". That comment is backwards, and it made every per-IP rate
 * limit on this platform a no-op. All Nxeon vhosts proxy with:
 *
 *     proxy_set_header X-Real-IP        $remote_addr;

content.content:
12224 docs/DOCUMENTATION.md
---tail---
branched off `main` in an isolated worktree (`/tank/dev-worktrees/fix-impersonation-bugs` — never
built against the live `/opt/nxeon` tree). Not pushed or deployed; committed to the branch only.

**Bug 1 — the customer's own Location/Sign-in IPs panel showed the ADMIN's city.** Root cause was
NOT the 2026-09-24 `UserSession` tracker (that model is unrelated to this panel) — the real source,
found by reading `app/admin/users/[id]/page.tsx`'s actual query, is the `Visit` model, written by
`app/api/track/route.ts` on every page view. That route attributes `Visit.userId` from
`currentUser()`, which is deliberately impersonation-aware (resolves to the TARGET customer) — but
`Visit.ip` is the PROXY-ATTESTED address of whoever's browser is actually making the request, which
never changes just because the signed-in identity did. While impersonating, every page view the
admin made wrote a `Visit` row under the customer's own `userId` with the admin's real IP/city,
which is exactly what the admin/users/[id] "Location"/"Sign-in IPs" panel renders straight from.
Fixed by checking `impersonating()` in `/api/track` and leaving `userId` null for the duration of
the grant — this isn't a real sign-in or session at all, so there's no correct non-null attribution
to fall back to; the admin's access is already correctly recorded by the existing
`admin.impersonate_start` AuditLog entry (`userId: admin.id`), so no second record was needed.

**Bug 2 — a ticket reply sent while impersonating was recorded and displayed as the customer's own
message.** `lib/reply-core.ts:writeTicketReply` computes `isStaff` from whatever actor identity it's
handed; `lib/actions-support.ts:requireTicketActor` resolved that via `requireUser()` →
`currentUser()`, which correctly-by-design returns the TARGET while impersonating — so a genuine
admin reply was indistinguishable from the customer's own. The admin ticket desk
(`/admin/support/[id]`) cannot be used as an alternate "real" reply surface instead: `app/admin/
layout.tsx` already refuses to render ANY `/admin/*` page while impersonating (`if (imp) redirect
("/dashboard")`), so the customer-facing form is the ONLY reply path reachable in that state at all.
Judgment call: `requireTicketActor` now checks `impersonating()` first and, if present, resolves to
the REAL admin underneath the grant (`lib/auth.ts`'s `impersonating()`, backed by the JWT's
`adminId`) with `isSupportStaff: true` — the exact same shape (`authorId` = the staff member's own
id, `isStaff: true`) a genuine `/admin/support` reply already produces, so this fix makes the
customer-facing path behave identically to the real staff tool rather than inventing a new
"impersonated reply" annotation.

**Bug 3 — leaving impersonation landed on a rendered "404 / Page not found" screen.**
`stopImpersonating()` cleared the cookie and called `redirect("/admin/users")`; this reproduced
LIVE and in a real Playwright browser run, but only against a genuine `next build` + `node .next/
standalone/server.js` (the exact way `nxeon-web.service` actually runs it) — never against `next
dev`, which disables the aggressive client-side Router Cache/prefetch layer production uses. Server-
side debug logging (temporarily added and removed) proved `app/admin/layout.tsx`'s own `impersonating
()` re-check is never even evaluated again as part of resolving this redirect, ruling out a stale-
cookie server-side re-render as the cause — yet the client's actual next request was for `/dashboard`
(confirmed via nginx's `next_action`-capturing forensic log on the real incident, and by the
`_rsc` token on the failing request in the Playwright trace), a page no longer reachable on the admin
host once impersonation is genuinely over, which is what produced the visible 404 while the URL bar
stayed on `/admin/users`. Rather than chase the exact Next.js production-router internal responsible,
the fix sidesteps it entirely: `stopImpersonating()` no longer calls `redirect()` itself (it now
only clears the cookie); the "Leave" button (`components/nx/Banners.tsx`'s `ImpersonationBanner`,
and the equivalent "Exit" control in `components/portal/Shell.tsx`) instead awaits the action and
then does a real `window.location.assign("/admin/users")` — a genuine top-level HTTP request no
client-side cache can ever misroute. Still unreachable by a prefetch or a crawler (same property the
old `<form action={...}>` comment called out — this is still gated behind a click that runs JS).

**Real, not just reasoned-about, verification.** Typecheck clean; full suite 1482 tests, 1445 passing
— the identical 37 pre-existing failures (unrelated pricing/proration/registrar tests), confirmed by
diffing the exact failing-test list before and after this branch's changes. Beyond unit tests: stood
up an isolated throwaway Postgres database and a real admin + real test-customer account, then drove
a genuine `next build` + standalone production server (the same binary `nxeon-web.service` runs) with
a real Chromium browser (Playwright) over real HTTPS (a local self-signed cert was required — the
session/impersonation cookies are hardcoded `secure: NODE_ENV==="production"`, so they're silently
dropped by the browser over plain http in a production build) end to end:
- Impersonated a real test customer; confirmed the "Client info" panel showed the CUSTOMER's real,
  older, seeded sign-in (Karachi) both before and after — no admin-IP row ever appeared — and
  confirmed directly in the database that the `Visit` rows written during the impersonated session
  carry `userId: null`, not the customer's id.
- Sent a real reply to the customer's own ticket via the customer-facing form while impersonating;
  confirmed directly in the database that `TicketMessage.authorId` is the ADMIN's own account,
  `authorRole: "ADMIN"`, `isStaff: true` — not the customer's id.
- Clicked "Leave"; confirmed the final page is the real `/admin/users` (the admin's own sidebar/nav,
  not a 404), the final URL matches, and the impersonation cookie is genuinely gone from the browser's
  cookie jar afterward.
- This exact sequence was first run against the UNFIXED code specifically to nail bug 3's mechanism
  (it 404'd, exactly as reported), then re-run against the fixed code (clean landing) — a real
  before/after, not just a single passing run.

**Files touched:** `app/api/track/route.ts`, `lib/actions-support.ts`, `lib/actions-account.ts`,
`components/nx/Banners.tsx`, `components/portal/Shell.tsx`.

---

*Companion docs: `CLAUDE.md` (agent/ops conventions), `ROADMAP.md` (backlog), `docs/MIGRATION.md`
(server migration).*

## Bandwidth and abuse detection
input.new_string:
- Tests: `/opt/nxeon/test/growth.test.ts`.

## Creator Partner Program — agency/KOL commission + a real customer discount

**What it does.** An agency or content creator gets a permanent link. Every customer who signs up
through it is attached to that partner FOR LIFE (one partner per customer, enforced by a DB unique
constraint) and gets a real, sitewide discount for as long as they stay a customer — **50% off their
first purchase of any service except a domain, then 10% off every purchase after that, forever**
(new orders AND renewals). The partner earns a **lifetime commission** (their own negotiated
`commissionRatePct`, default 20%) on every qualifying charge that customer ever makes, with one
carve-out: a dedicated-IP add-on line earns the partner 0% (everything else on the same
order/renewal still earns the full rate).

This is a DIFFERENT program from "Refer & earn" (`User.referralCode`, the row above this one) — a
peer-to-peer, one-time wallet bonus. A single `?ref=`/`nxeon_ref` cookie can only ever mean ONE of
the two: at registration (`lib/actions.ts` `register()`), an ACTIVE `ReferralPartner.code` match
always wins over a `User.referralCode` match, so nobody double-dips a partner commission AND a peer
referral bonus off the same signup.

**Data model** (`prisma/schema.prisma`):

| Model | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ReferralPartner` | The partner: `code` (unique, uppercase), `commissionRatePct` (per-partner, frozen onto each commission row at accrual), `status` (ACTIVE/PAUSED — pausing stops BOTH new commission AND the customer discount), optional `userId` login |
| `PartnerCustomer` | The lifetime attachment. `customerId` UNIQUE — one partner per customer, ever. `firstPurchaseDiscountUsedAt` (null until their first discounted purchase; null = 50% tier, set = 10% tier forever) |
| `PartnerCommission` | One row per qualifying PAID invoice, `invoiceId` UNIQUE (idempotent). `baseCents` = net charge minus that invoice's `dedicatedIpCents` — the dedicated-IP exclusion |
| `PartnerPayout` | A REAL payment made to the partner off-wallet (bank/Wise/PayPal), can be partial. Balance = `sum(PartnerCommission, status != VOID) − sum(PartnerPayout)` — NOT derived from commission-row status alone (see the model's own doc comment for why a partial payout needs a separate ledger) |
| `PartnerInvite` | A pending invite for a brand-new (non-customer) partner login — token-hash/expiry, mirrors `OrgInvite`'s mechanics |
| `ReferralClick` (existing, previously unused) | One row per real link click — `code`, `ipHash`, `referer`, `convertedUserId` (best-effort, set at registration to the most recent unconverted click for that code) |
| `Invoice.dedicatedIpCents` | How much of that invoice's net amount is the dedicated-IP surcharge — a real typed column, populated by every charge path that can bill one (`lib/order.ts`, `lib/game-order.ts`, `worker/billing.ts`), never inferred by parsing line items after the fact |

**The links.** `nxeon.cloud/partner/<code>` (`app/partner/[code]/route.ts`) is the REAL link partners
are given — it records a `ReferralClick` row, then sets the `nxeon_ref` cookie and 302s to
`/register`, exactly like the older `/r/<code>` (peer-referral short link), which now ALSO records a
click (same table — its own schema comment always said it covers both code namespaces).

**Automatic attachment.** `register()` (`lib/actions.ts`) reads `nxeon_ref`; if it matches an ACTIVE
partner code, `attachCustomerToPartnerByCode` (`lib/partner-commission.ts`) creates the
`PartnerCustomer` row right there — no admin action needed for the normal case. `adminAttachCustomer`
(`lib/actions-partner.ts`) remains for support/edge cases (attaching an existing account by email).

**The customer discount** — pure math in `lib/partner-discount.ts` (`PARTNER_FIRST_PURCHASE_PCT` =
50, `PARTNER_RECURRING_PCT` = 10), DB resolution in `lib/partner-pricing.ts`
(`partnerDiscountForNewOrder`, `partnerDiscountForRenewal`, `partnerPreviewForCode`/`ForUser` for
pre-purchase marketing messaging). Wired into:
- `lib/order.ts` `orderQuote`/`placeOrder` (VPS) and `lib/game-order.ts` `gameOrderQuote`/
  `placeGameOrder` (game servers) — the discount is folded into `chargeCents` itself (displayed ===
  charged), gets its OWN line on the invoice, and the first-purchase slot is claimed ATOMICALLY
  inside the same transaction that debits the wallet (`claimPartnerFirstPurchase`) — a lost race (the
  same customer's own concurrent "first" order) keeps the already-quoted price rather than
  recomputing mid-transaction (an accepted, narrow, low-severity edge case: a customer can only ever
  race against their OWN other order).
- `lib/renewal-charge.ts` `renewalCharge` — `RenewalPrices.partnerDiscountPercent` (optional, 0 by
  default), always resolved via `partnerDiscountForRenewal` (a renewal is never anyone's first
  purchase), stacks with the pre-existing one-time retention offer (retention first, partner discount
  on what's left). Wired into every real renewal path in `worker/billing.ts` (the automatic sweep,
  the saved-card auto-charge, the renewal-reminder email amount, the suspended-account
  auto-recovery) and `lib/actions.ts` `renewNow`.
- **Visible before the first purchase**, per the product requirement: the public `/pricing` page
  reads the `nxeon_ref` cookie (anonymous) or the real attachment (signed in) and shows a real banner;
  the deploy wizard (`components/nx/DeployView.tsx`) shows a live "Partner discount — 50%/10% off"
  badge next to the coupon/promo badges, sourced from the same `orderQuote`/`gameOrderQuote` result
  the wizard already prices from (`lib/nx/quote.ts`, `lib/nx/quote-game.ts`) — not a second formula.
- **Hosting, business email and domains do NOT carry this discount yet** (domains are excluded by
  spec; hosting/email have no coupon-style discount plumbing to extend today) — a real, flagged
  follow-up, not silently missing (the wizard's price object honestly reports 0%/NONE for them).

**Commission dedicated-IP exclusion** — `commissionableBaseCents(netCents, dedicatedIpCents)`
(`lib/partner-commission.ts`, pure, unit-tested) = `max(0, netCents − dedicatedIpCents)`. Every
accrual path (`accrueCommissionForInvoice`, called by the inline post-order/post-renewal hooks AND
the background `reconcilePartnerCommissions` sweep) reads `Invoice.dedicatedIpCents` and excludes it
— never a string match against a line-item description.

**Admin** (`/admin/partners`, `/admin/partners/[id]`, `lib/actions-partner.ts`,
`components/admin/PartnerControls.tsx`): create/manage partners and rates (existing), attach/detach
customers (existing), plus new: real click→signup→conversion funnel (`partnerFunnel`), the real
`/partner/<code>` link, **invite a brand-new login** (`adminCreatePartnerInvite` — a public accept
page at `/partner/invite/accept?token=...` creates the account, since the invitee has none yet;
mirrors `OrgInvite`'s token/hash/expiry, not its `requireUser()`-gated redemption), and **record a
partial/specific payout** (`adminRecordPartnerPayout`) alongside the existing full-settle
(`adminSettlePartnerCommission`, now payout-ledger-aware).

**Partner portal** (`/dashboard/partner`, `components/nx/PartnerView.tsx`): unchanged sections
(customers, commission ledger) plus new: real click/signup/conversion stats, the real `/partner/
<code>` link, a payout-history table, a media kit (downloads the app's own real `/logo.png`, `/
nx-mark.png`, `/brand/bimi-logo.svg`, plus two new on-brand promo SVG banners at `/brand/partner/`),
and a terms panel stating the partner's REAL `commissionRatePct` (never a hardcoded blanket rate —
partners are on genuinely different negotiated rates) and that payout method/minimum is not yet
configured platform-wide (nothing invented).

**Tests.** `test/partner-discount.test.ts` — pure arithmetic, no DB: discount tier resolution (not
attached / paused partner / domain → NONE; first purchase → 50%; used → 10%), the dedicated-IP
commission-exclusion boundary cases (IP-only order, mixed-addon order, no-IP order, corrupt/negative

## Creator Partner Program — agency/KOL commission + a real customer discount

**What it does.** An agency or content creator gets a permanent link. Every customer who signs up
through it is attached to that partner FOR LIFE (one partner per customer, enforced by a DB unique
constraint) and gets a real, sitewide discount for as long as they stay a customer — **50% off their
first purchase of any service except a domain, then 10% off every purchase after that, forever**
(new orders AND renewals). The partner earns a **lifetime commission** (their own negotiated
`commissionRatePct`, default 20%) on every qualifying charge that customer ever makes, with one
carve-out: a dedicated-IP add-on line earns the partner 0% (everything else on the same
order/renewal still earns the full rate).

This is a DIFFERENT program from "Refer & earn" (`User.referralCode`, the row above this one) — a
peer-to-peer, one-time wallet bonus. A single `?ref=`/`nxeon_ref` cookie can only ever mean ONE of
the two: at registration (`lib/actions.ts` `register()`), an ACTIVE `ReferralPartner.code` match
always wins over a `User.referralCode` match, so nobody double-dips a partner commission AND a peer
referral bonus off the same signup.

**Data model** (`prisma/schema.prisma`):

| Model | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ReferralPartner` | The partner: `code` (unique, uppercase), `commissionRatePct` (per-partner, frozen onto each commission row at accrual), `status` (ACTIVE/PAUSED — pausing stops BOTH new commission AND the customer discount), optional `userId` login |
| `PartnerCustomer` | The lifetime attachment. `customerId` UNIQUE — one partner per customer, ever. `firstPurchaseDiscountUsedAt` (null until their first discounted purchase; null = 50% tier, set = 10% tier forever) |
| `PartnerCommission` | One row per qualifying PAID invoice, `invoiceId` UNIQUE (idempotent). `baseCents` = net charge minus that invoice's `dedicatedIpCents` — the dedicated-IP exclusion |
| `PartnerPayout` | A REAL payment made to the partner off-wallet (bank/Wise/PayPal), can be partial. Balance = `sum(PartnerCommission, status != VOID) − sum(PartnerPayout)` — NOT derived from commission-row status alone (see the model's own doc comment for why a partial payout needs a separate ledger) |
| `PartnerInvite` | A pending invite for a brand-new (non-customer) partner login — token-hash/expiry, mirrors `OrgInvite`'s mechanics |
| `ReferralClick` (existing, previously unused) | One row per real link click — `code`, `ipHash`, `referer`, `convertedUserId` (best-effort, set at registration to the most recent unconverted click for that code) |
| `Invoice.dedicatedIpCents` | How much of that invoice's net amount is the dedicated-IP surcharge — a real typed column, populated by every charge path that can bill one (`lib/order.ts`, `lib/game-order.ts`, `worker/billing.ts`), never inferred by parsing line items after the fact |

**The links.** `nxeon.cloud/partner/<code>` (`app/partner/[code]/route.ts`) is the REAL link partners
are given — it records a `ReferralClick` row, then sets the `nxeon_ref` cookie and 302s to
`/register`, exactly like the older `/r/<code>` (peer-referral short link), which now ALSO records a
click (same table — its own schema comment always said it covers both code namespaces).

**Automatic attachment.** `register()` (`lib/actions.ts`) reads `nxeon_ref`; if it matches an ACTIVE
partner code, `attachCustomerToPartnerByCode` (`lib/partner-commission.ts`) creates the
`PartnerCustomer` row right there — no admin action needed for the normal case. `adminAttachCustomer`
(`lib/actions-partner.ts`) remains for support/edge cases (attaching an existing account by email).

**The customer discount** — pure math in `lib/partner-discount.ts` (`PARTNER_FIRST_PURCHASE_PCT` =
50, `PARTNER_RECURRING_PCT` = 10), DB resolution in `lib/partner-pricing.ts`
(`partnerDiscountForNewOrder`, `partnerDiscountForRenewal`, `partnerPreviewForCode`/`ForUser` for
pre-purchase marketing messaging). Wired into:
- `lib/order.ts` `orderQuote`/`placeOrder` (VPS) and `lib/game-order.ts` `gameOrderQuote`/
  `placeGameOrder` (game servers) — the discount is folded into `chargeCents` itself (displayed ===
  charged), gets its OWN line on the invoice, and the first-purchase slot is claimed ATOMICALLY
  inside the same transaction that debits the wallet (`claimPartnerFirstPurchase`) — a lost race (the
  same customer's own concurrent "first" order) keeps the already-quoted price rather than
  recomputing mid-transaction (an accepted, narrow, low-severity edge case: a customer can only ever
  race against their OWN other order).
- `lib/renewal-charge.ts` `renewalCharge` — `RenewalPrices.partnerDiscountPercent` (optional, 0 by
  default), always resolved via `partnerDiscountForRenewal` (a renewal is never anyone's first
  purchase), stacks with the pre-existing one-time retention offer (retention first, partner discount
  on what's left). Wired into every real renewal path in `worker/billing.ts` (the automatic sweep,

  transaction. Visible before checkout on the public pricing page and live in

  earns their full rate - required a new typed Invoice.dedicatedIpCents column

admin setting anywhere in this codebase, so the terms panel says so honestly.

commission exclusion, cross-checked against the real admin dashboard.
EOF

**Branch**: `feature/creator-partner-program` in worktree `/root/nxeon-worktrees/creator-partner-program`, one commit (`2732814569`), NOT pushed to origin, production (`/opt/nxeon`) untouched and confirmed clean.

This pass built everything genuinely missing: the customer discount, real click tracking, the dedicated-IP commission exclusion, partner-login invites, and partial payouts.

**What's real and verified:**
- **Schema** (additive, `prisma db push`-safe): `Invoice.dedicatedIpCents`, `PartnerCustomer.firstPurchaseDiscountUsedAt`, new `PartnerPayout` and `PartnerInvite` models. Wired up the pre-existing, previously-unused `ReferralClick` table for click tracking rather than inventing a new one.

Visible pre-purchase on `/pricing` and live in the deploy wizard badge.
